subject: CC
stem: Which method is considered the reference method for glucose determination?
explanation: The hexokinase method is the reference method because it is highly specific and less affected by interferences than glucose oxidase. Folin-Wu and o-toluidine are older, less specific methods. Reference: StatPearls, Hexokinase Method (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK587446).

subject: CC
stem: Which enzyme is the most specific marker for acute pancreatitis?
explanation: Lipase is more specific to the pancreas than amylase and stays elevated longer after an attack of acute pancreatitis. Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Lipase (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537346).

subject: CC
stem: Which lipoprotein carries most of the cholesterol to peripheral tissues?
explanation: LDL delivers cholesterol to peripheral cells (the 'bad' cholesterol). HDL does reverse cholesterol transport back to the liver. Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Cholesterol (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK513326).

subject: CC
stem: Which formula correctly computes the anion gap (without potassium)?
explanation: Anion gap = Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). When potassium is included it becomes (Na⁺ + K⁺) − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). Reference: StatPearls, Biochemistry, Anion Gap (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539757).

subject: CC
stem: The Jaffe reaction for creatinine uses which reagent?
explanation: In the Jaffe reaction, creatinine reacts with alkaline picrate to form a red-orange complex. Diacetyl monoxime is for urea, phosphotungstic acid for uric acid, and o-cresolphthalein for calcium. Reference: Peake & Whiting, Measurement of Serum Creatinine, Clin Biochem Rev 2006 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1784008).

subject: CC
stem: What is the best initial screening test for suspected primary thyroid dysfunction?
explanation: TSH is the most sensitive indicator of thyroid dysfunction, so it is the first-line screening test; free T4 is added when TSH is abnormal. Reference: StatPearls, Physiology, Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499850).

subject: CC
stem: In healthy adults, serum cortisol is normally highest:
choices: In the early morning, soon after waking
explanation: Cortisol follows a 24-hour (circadian) rhythm: it peaks in the early morning after waking and is lowest around midnight, so the collection time matters. Reference: Development of 24-Hour Rhythms in Cortisol Secretion, meta-analysis (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11747683).

subject: CC
stem: In Westgard multirule quality control, the 1-3s rule is violated when:
choices: Two consecutive controls exceed the same ±2SD limit
One control result falls outside the mean ±3SD
One control exceeds +2SD and another exceeds −2SD in the same run
Ten consecutive results fall on one side of the mean
explanation: 1-3s = a single control beyond ±3SD. It is a rejection rule and usually points to random error. 2-2s detects systematic error, R-4s random error within a run, and 10x a shift. Reference: Westgard QC, Westgard Rules (westgard.com/westgard-rules.html).

subject: CC
stem: According to Beer's law, the absorbance of a solution is:
choices: Directly proportional to its concentration and the light path length
Independent of the light path length
explanation: A = εbc: absorbance rises linearly with concentration and path length, so a plot of absorbance against concentration is a straight line through zero (it bends at high concentrations). Reference: Chemistry LibreTexts, Beer-Lambert Law (chem.libretexts.org, Organic Chemistry Glossary).

subject: CC
stem: An AST:ALT ratio of 2:1 or higher most suggests:
explanation: AST rises more than ALT in alcohol-related liver disease, so an AST:ALT ratio of 2:1 or more points to it. Reference: StatPearls, Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK562172) and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK546632).

subject: CC
stem: Which enzyme rises most markedly in biliary (obstructive) liver disease?
explanation: A marked rise in alkaline phosphatase, with normal or only mildly raised transaminases, points to biliary obstruction. Reference: StatPearls, Hyperbilirubinemia (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK544252).

subject: CC
stem: The most abundant protein in human plasma is:
explanation: Albumin makes up about half of total plasma protein (3.5–5 g/dL) and most of the plasma oncotic pressure. Reference: StatPearls, Physiology, Albumin (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459198).

subject: CC
stem: The biuret method for total protein is based on:
choices: Aromatic amino acids absorbing light at 280 nm
Peptide bonds forming a violet complex with Cu²⁺ in alkaline solution
Free amino groups reacting with ninhydrin
explanation: In alkaline solution, cupric ions bind the nitrogens of peptide bonds and turn violet; free amino acids do not react. It is simple but relatively insensitive. Reference: Biology LibreTexts, Fundamentals of Biochemistry, 3.3 Proteins: Analyses and Structural Predictions (bio.libretexts.org).

subject: CC
stem: In therapeutic drug monitoring, a trough level is collected:
choices: At the time of peak absorption
Exactly 1 hour after an IV dose
explanation: The trough is the lowest concentration, reached just before the next dose; the peak reflects maximum absorption. Reference: Overview of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2687654).

subject: CC
stem: Carbon monoxide is toxic mainly because it:
choices: Oxidizes heme iron to the ferric state
Binds hemoglobin about 200–250 times more strongly than oxygen
explanation: CO forms carboxyhemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen. Oxidized (ferric) heme iron is methemoglobin, and acetylcholinesterase inhibition is the mechanism of organophosphates. Reference: StatPearls, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557888).

subject: CC
stem: A fasting plasma glucose diagnostic of diabetes mellitus is:
explanation: ADA criteria: FPG 126 mg/dL or higher (7.0 mmol/L). FPG 100 to 125 mg/dL is impaired fasting glucose (prediabetes). Reference: American Diabetes Association, 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026 (diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926).

subject: CC
stem: An HbA1c result diagnostic of diabetes is:
explanation: ADA criteria: A1C 6.5% or higher (48 mmol/mol). A1C 5.7% to 6.4% is prediabetes. Reference: American Diabetes Association, 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026 (diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926).

subject: CC
stem: In a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test, a 2-hour plasma glucose diagnostic of diabetes is:
explanation: ADA criteria: 2-hour plasma glucose 200 mg/dL or higher during a 75-g OGTT. 140 to 199 mg/dL is impaired glucose tolerance. Reference: American Diabetes Association, 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026 (diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926).

subject: CC
stem: Glucagon is produced by which pancreatic islet cells?
explanation: Alpha cells produce glucagon, which raises blood glucose; beta cells produce insulin. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.9 The Endocrine Pancreas (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-9-the-endocrine-pancreas).

subject: CC
stem: Whipple's triad is used to confirm:
explanation: Whipple's triad is symptoms of hypoglycemia, a low blood glucose at the time, and relief of symptoms when glucose is raised. Reference: Investigation and Causes of Spontaneous (Non-Diabetic) Hypoglycaemia in Adults: Pitfalls to Avoid (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10606153).

subject: CC
stem: High insulin with LOW C-peptide in a hypoglycemic patient suggests:
explanation: Taking too much insulin suppresses the pancreas, so C-peptide (made with the body's own insulin) is low. Insulinoma raises C-peptide. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, C-Peptide Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/c-peptide-test).

subject: CC
stem: The Friedewald formula for LDL cholesterol is NOT valid when triglycerides exceed:
explanation: The Friedewald equation cannot be applied when triglyceride levels exceed 400 mg/dL; a direct LDL assay or another equation is used instead. Reference: Comparative Evaluation of 24 LDL-C Estimation Equations Against Direct Assays (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12468580).

subject: CC
stem: The Friedewald formula (mg/dL) is:
explanation: Friedewald estimates VLDL cholesterol with the fixed factor TG/5 (mg/dL), so LDL = total cholesterol - HDL - TG/5. Reference: Comparative Evaluation of 24 LDL-C Estimation Equations Against Direct Assays (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12468580).

subject: CC
stem: Which lipoprotein carries cholesterol from the tissues back to the liver?
explanation: HDL, through its main protein apoA-I, carries out reverse cholesterol transport: returning cholesterol from tissues to the liver. Reference: A narrative review of impacts of apolipoproteins on atherosclerotic coronary plaques (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12912438).

subject: CC
stem: The main apolipoprotein of LDL is:
explanation: ApoB-100 is found on VLDL, IDL and LDL; its shorter form apoB-48 is found only on chylomicrons. ApoA-I is the main protein of HDL. Reference: Closing the gaps in patient management of dyslipidemia: apolipoprotein profiling (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10908091); A narrative review of impacts of apolipoproteins on atherosclerotic coronary plaques (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12912438).

subject: CC
stem: Lipoprotein lipase is activated by:
explanation: ApoC-II is the co-factor for lipoprotein lipase on triglyceride-rich lipoproteins; apoC-III inhibits it. Reference: A Pressure-dependent Model for the Regulation of Lipoprotein Lipase by Apolipoprotein C-II (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4505049).

subject: CC
stem: On serum protein electrophoresis, the largest peak, closest to the positive electrode (anode), is:
explanation: Albumin is the largest peak and lies closest to the positive electrode, followed by alpha-1, alpha-2, beta and gamma globulins. Reference: O'Connell et al., Understanding and Interpreting Serum Protein Electrophoresis, AFP 2005 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2005/0101/p105.html).

subject: CC
stem: A sharp, narrow spike (M-spike) in the gamma region suggests:
choices: A monoclonal gammopathy such as multiple myeloma
explanation: A homogeneous spike-like peak in the gamma zone indicates a monoclonal gammopathy such as multiple myeloma. Reference: O'Connell et al., Understanding and Interpreting Serum Protein Electrophoresis, AFP 2005 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2005/0101/p105.html).

subject: CC
stem: On serum protein electrophoresis, cirrhosis is listed among conditions that increase:
explanation: Cirrhosis is among the diseases that raise the gamma-globulin level (a polyclonal increase), while albumin tends to fall from poor synthesis. Reference: O'Connell et al., Understanding and Interpreting Serum Protein Electrophoresis, AFP 2005 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2005/0101/p105.html).

subject: CC
stem: In nephrotic syndrome, SPE shows decreased albumin with a markedly increased:
explanation: Albumin falls from renal loss in nephrotic syndrome, which is also listed among causes of increased alpha-2 globulins. Reference: O'Connell et al., Understanding and Interpreting Serum Protein Electrophoresis, AFP 2005 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2005/0101/p105.html).

subject: CC
stem: A missing or faint alpha-1 band on SPE suggests deficiency of:
explanation: The alpha-1 fraction consists of alpha-1 antitrypsin with thyroid-binding globulin and transcortin, so alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency gives a faint band. Reference: O'Connell et al., Understanding and Interpreting Serum Protein Electrophoresis, AFP 2005 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2005/0101/p105.html).

subject: CC
stem: Decreased serum ceruloplasmin is characteristic of:
explanation: Low ceruloplasmin may be a sign of Wilson disease, although levels are sometimes normal in this disease. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Ceruloplasmin Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ceruloplasmin-test).

subject: CC
stem: CK-BB (CK-1) is found mainly in the:
explanation: High CK-MM suggests skeletal muscle damage, high CK-MB heart muscle damage, and high CK-BB a stroke or brain injury. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Creatine Kinase (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/creatine-kinase).

subject: CC
stem: The most specific laboratory marker of myocardial injury is:
explanation: Troponin testing is better than CK at finding heart muscle damage from a heart attack, and it is mainly used to help diagnose heart attacks. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Creatine Kinase (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/creatine-kinase).

subject: CC
stem: Which enzyme rises in cholestatic liver disease but stays normal in bone disease?
explanation: GGT is raised in cholestatic disorders but not in bone disease, so a high ALP with high GGT points to a hepatobiliary source. Reference: Gowda et al., A review on laboratory liver function tests (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2984286); A Systematic Approach to Patients with Jaundice (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5088098).

subject: CC
stem: A competitive inhibitor:
choices: Competes with the substrate for the active site
Binds only to the enzyme-substrate complex
explanation: A competitive inhibitor competes with the substrate for binding at the active site, so adding more substrate can overcome it. Reference: OpenStax Biology 2e, 6.5 Enzymes (openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes).

subject: CC
stem: Urea nitrogen (BUN) is a waste product formed from the breakdown of:
explanation: Urea nitrogen is a waste product that forms as the body breaks down proteins; the kidneys remove it. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen) (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/bun-blood-urea-nitrogen).

subject: CC
stem: Uric acid is the end product of the breakdown of:
explanation: Uric acid is a normal waste product made when the body breaks down purines. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Uric Acid Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/uric-acid-test).

subject: CC
stem: A BUN:creatinine ratio above 20:1 with normal creatinine suggests:
explanation: Prerenal failure shows a bland urine sediment, urine osmolality above 500 mOsm and a BUN-to-creatinine ratio above 20:1. Reference: Agrawal & Swartz, Acute Renal Failure, AFP 2000 (aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2000/0401/p2077.html).

subject: CC
stem: In the body, ammonia is converted into urea mainly by the:
explanation: Liver enzymes turn ammonia into urea, which the kidneys then excrete. Liver disease damages this ability. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Ammonia Levels (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ammonia-levels).

subject: CC
stem: The major INTRACELLULAR cation is:
explanation: Almost all of the body's potassium is inside the cells. Sodium is the major extracellular cation. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Potassium Blood Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/potassium-blood-test).

subject: CC
stem: Freezing point depression is a colligative property, meaning it depends on:
choices: The concentration of dissolved solute particles
explanation: Freezing point depression is directly proportional to the molal concentration of solute particles. This is why it can be used to measure osmolality. Reference: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, 11.4 Colligative Properties (openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/11-4-colligative-properties).

subject: CC
stem: Which fraction of serum calcium is physiologically active?
explanation: Ionized (free) calcium is the form active in body functions; protein-bound and free calcium are normally present in about equal amounts. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Calcium Blood Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/calcium-blood-test).

subject: CC
stem: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium partly by:
choices: Stimulating osteoclasts to release calcium from bone
explanation: PTH stimulates osteoclasts to release calcium from bone and increases calcium reabsorption in the kidney tubules. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.5 The Parathyroid Glands (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-5-the-parathyroid-glands).

subject: CC
stem: At normal blood pH, the ratio of bicarbonate to carbonic acid is about:
explanation: Bicarbonate and carbonic acid are present in the blood in a 20:1 ratio when blood pH is within the normal range. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 26.4 Acid-Base Balance (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/26-4-acid-base-balance).

subject: CC
stem: Bilirubin is conjugated in the liver by:
explanation: UDP-glucuronyltransferase converts bilirubin into conjugated mono- and diglucuronides; genetic defects of this enzyme cause Gilbert and Crigler-Najjar syndromes. Reference: Gowda et al., A review on laboratory liver function tests (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2984286).

subject: CC
stem: Biliverdin is converted to bilirubin by:
explanation: The non-iron part of heme becomes biliverdin, which is then reduced to bilirubin by biliverdin reductase. Reference: A Systematic Approach to Patients with Jaundice (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5088098); OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/18-3-erythrocytes).

subject: CC
stem: Dubin-Johnson syndrome causes which type of hyperbilirubinemia?
explanation: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia without liver injury is seen in Dubin-Johnson and Rotor syndromes. Absent UDP-glucuronyltransferase (Crigler-Najjar) gives unconjugated bilirubin. Reference: A Systematic Approach to Patients with Jaundice (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5088098); Gowda et al., A review on laboratory liver function tests (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2984286).

subject: CC
stem: In hemolysis, serum bilirubin rises mainly because of:
choices: Overproduction of bilirubin without true liver injury
explanation: Bilirubin overproduction is commonly seen without any true liver injury, as in hemolysis, raising mainly unconjugated bilirubin. Reference: A Systematic Approach to Patients with Jaundice (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5088098).

subject: CC
stem: The normal brown color of stool comes from:
explanation: Bilirubin is secreted in bile and broken down in the gut; stercobilins in feces produce the typical brown color. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/18-3-erythrocytes).

subject: CC
stem: Hepatic encephalopathy is associated with increased blood:
explanation: In hepatic encephalopathy, toxins including ammonia build up in the brain because the liver cannot break them down. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Ammonia Levels (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ammonia-levels).

subject: CC
stem: Primary hypothyroidism shows:
explanation: When thyroid hormone is too low, the pituitary makes more TSH, so primary (thyroid) failure gives high TSH with low T4. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone) Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test); OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.4 The Thyroid Gland (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-4-the-thyroid-gland).

subject: CC
stem: Graves disease is caused by antibodies that:
explanation: Graves disease, the most common cause of hyperthyroidism, is an autoimmune reaction in which antibodies overstimulate the thyroid follicle cells. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.4 The Thyroid Gland (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-4-the-thyroid-gland); MedlinePlus Lab Tests, TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone) Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test).

subject: CC
stem: Cushing syndrome is caused by excess:
explanation: Cushing syndrome is caused by hypersecretion of cortisol, giving high cortisol levels. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.6 The Adrenal Glands (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-6-the-adrenal-glands); MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Cortisol Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cortisol-test).

subject: CC
stem: Addison disease is caused by:
explanation: Addison disease (chronic adrenal insufficiency) is hyposecretion of corticosteroids, with low cortisol and reduced aldosterone. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.6 The Adrenal Glands (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-6-the-adrenal-glands); MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Cortisol Test (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cortisol-test); OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 26.4 Acid-Base Balance (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/26-4-acid-base-balance).

subject: CC
stem: Which test is used to screen for pheochromocytoma?
explanation: Catecholamine tests are used to diagnose or rule out rare tumors such as pheochromocytoma, a tumor of the adrenal glands. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Catecholamine Tests (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/catecholamine-tests).

subject: CC
stem: Diabetes insipidus results from deficiency of, or resistance to:
explanation: Diabetes insipidus is characterized by chronic underproduction of ADH, so the kidneys do not reabsorb enough water. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.3 The Pituitary Gland and Hypothalamus (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-3-the-pituitary-gland-and-hypothalamus).

subject: CC
stem: The major mineralocorticoid hormone of the adrenal cortex is:
explanation: Aldosterone is the major mineralocorticoid; the renin-angiotensin system signals the adrenal cortex to secrete it. Reference: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.6 The Adrenal Glands (openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/17-6-the-adrenal-glands).

subject: CC
stem: An acetaminophen overdose mainly damages the:
explanation: Too much acetaminophen can cause serious and sometimes deadly liver damage, which is why levels are checked after an overdose. Reference: MedlinePlus Lab Tests, Acetaminophen Level (medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/acetaminophen-level).

subject: CC
stem: A common and often permanent effect of methanol poisoning is:
explanation: Blindness is common and often permanent after methanol poisoning, despite medical care. Reference: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia, Methanol poisoning (medlineplus.gov/ency/article/002680.htm).

subject: CC
stem: The Westgard 2-2s rule (two consecutive controls beyond the same 2 SD limit) mainly detects:
explanation: The 2-2s rule is responsive only to systematic error (a shift in the mean), and it is not very sensitive by itself. Reference: Westgard QC, Abuses, Misuses, and In-excuses (westgard.com/lessons/westgard-rules/westgard-rules/lesson73.html).

subject: CC
stem: The R-4s rule (two controls in a run differ by more than 4 SD) indicates:
explanation: R-4s is a rule for random error and should be used only within a run, to tell random error from between-run systematic error. Reference: Westgard QC, Abuses, Misuses, and In-excuses (westgard.com/lessons/westgard-rules/westgard-rules/lesson73.html).
